To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CdS nanocrystal/polymer nanocomposites have been prepared by an in situ growth process of CdS nanocrystallites in a semiconducting polymer.
CdS/MEHLPPV nanocomposite films have been obtained by in situ thermolytically growing CdS nanocrystallites in the polymer.
we have developed a new synthetic route to fabricating nanocomposites of MEH-PPVs and CdS NCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of well-dispersing CdS NCs in semiconductors, with the aim of developing hybrid nanocomposite materials for optoelectronics.
the development of new strategies to obtain well-dispersed NCs in semiconductors polymers, in a straight synthetic route, by means of in situ thermolytical processes.
the development of a straight synthetic route to obtain well-dispersed NCs in a polymer host.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CdS NCs in MEH-PPVs are well dispersed, homogeneously distributed and the photoluminescence of the NCs is quenched, thus indicating that the CdS NCs have been well embedded into the polymer matrix and that they do not aggregate.

the use of a soluble cadmium complex as starting reagent allows the preparation of well-dispersing CdS NCs in a semiconducting polymer matrix, with the advantage of avoiding the use of a toxic and corrosive cadmium salt.
this is a simple synthetic route to fabricating well-dispersed nanocomposites of CdS NCs in a semiconducting polymer matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CdS NCs can be grown inside MEH- PPV matrix with a high yield, without the need for post-synthesis purification and with a high control of the size and morphology of CdS NCs.
the CdS NCs growth is a thermolytic process, in which the cadmium bis(thiolate) precursor is the source of cadmium and sulfur, while the Lewis base is the source of the sulfide ions.
the use of a soluble precursor allows the in situ growth of CdS NCs in a polymer matrix, with a simple synthetic route and a good control on the final morphology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CdS NCs can be grown in situ in a wide variety of polymers and that the resulting nanocomposites have a very good stability in the solid state.

the in situ thermolytically process can be used to prepare nanocomposite films containing a wide variety of NCs in a wide variety of polymers, provided that the precursor is soluble in the chosen polymer.
a simple and versatile synthetic route is proposed to obtain nanocrystalline semiconductor NCs embedded in a polymer matrix.
